sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《难以察觉》（99% Invisible）。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: It's really hard to get a sound trademarked.
sentences.zh: 给声音注册商标其实非常难。

sentences.en: The first one in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国的第一例声音商标

sentences.en: was issued in 1978 to NBC for their chimes.
sentences.zh: 是在1978年颁发给全国广播公司（NBC）的，作为他们的台钟声。

sentences.en: MGM has one for their roaring lion.
sentences.zh: 米高梅影业有一个咆哮狮子的声音商标。

sentences.en: As does 20th Century Fox.
sentences.zh: 二十世纪福斯也是如此。

sentences.en: That's 99PI's own Katie Mingle, TM.
sentences.zh: 那是99PI自己的凯蒂·明格，商标持有者。

sentences.en: Harley Davidson famously tried to trademark the sound of their motorcycles.
sentences.zh: 哈雷戴维森曾因试图为摩托车的引擎声注册商标而闻名。

sentences.en: That potato, potato, potato sound.
sentences.zh: 那种“突突突”的声音。

sentences.en: After years of litigation, they finally withdrew their application.
sentences.zh: 经过多年的诉讼，他们最终撤回了申请。

sentences.en: So if a bunch of burly bikers can't do it, it must be really hard.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一群魁梧的机车手都做不到，那这肯定非常难。

sentences.en: Right now, there are fewer than 200 active trademarks for sounds,
sentences.zh: 目前，有效的声音商标不到200个，

sentences.en: even though sound can be super important to brand.
sentences.zh: 尽管声音对品牌来说超级重要。

sentences.en: Just ask these guys.
sentences.zh: 问问这些人就知道了。

sentences.en: My name is Joel Beckerman.
sentences.zh: 我叫乔尔·贝克曼。

sentences.en: And I'm Tyler Gray.
sentences.zh: 我是泰勒·格雷。

sentences.en: Tyler and I wrote a book called The Sonic Boom,
sentences.zh: 我和泰勒合著了一本书，名叫《声爆》，

sentences.en: How Sound Transforms the Way We Think, Feel, and Buy.
sentences.zh: 副标题是《声音如何改变我们的思考、感受和购买方式》。

sentences.en: Here's a sound that would be, like, impossible to trademark.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个听起来几乎不可能注册商标的声音。

sentences.en: But Tyler and Joel say it was crucial to building up the brand it's associated with.
sentences.zh: 但泰勒和乔尔说，它对建立与之相关的品牌至关重要。

sentences.en: Oh man, I know that sound.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我知道那个声音。

sentences.en: I know it so well.
sentences.zh: 我太熟悉了。

sentences.en: When I was just a little kid on a cul-de-sac, they built a Chili's in my town.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个住在死胡同里的小孩时，我的小镇上开了一家奇利餐厅（Chili's）。

sentences.en: This was before there were really chain restaurants where I lived.
sentences.zh: 这在我住的地方出现连锁餐厅之前。

sentences.en: So Chili's actually felt kind of novel and exotic.
sentences.zh: 所以奇利餐厅当时感觉挺新奇、挺有异国情调的。

sentences.en: My family was pumped.
sentences.zh: 我的家人兴奋极了。

sentences.en: And our favorite thing to order?
sentences.zh: 我们最喜欢点什么呢？

sentences.en: The fajitas.
sentences.zh: 法士达（Fajitas）。

sentences.en: They don't really sell the steak.
sentences.zh: 他们卖的其实不是牛排。

sentences.en: They sell the sizzle.
sentences.zh: 他们卖的是滋滋声。

sentences.en: In their book, Joel and Tyler use Chili's and their sizzling fajitas
sentences.zh: 在他们的书中，乔尔和泰勒将奇利餐厅及其滋滋作响的法士达

sentences.en: as an opening example to illustrate why companies should think more about sound.
sentences.zh: 作为开篇例子，来说明为什么公司应该更多地考虑声音。

sentences.en: You're sitting in a Chili's at the dinner hour at 5 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 你正坐在晚上5点晚餐时间的奇利餐厅里。

sentences.en: And let's say at first nobody's ordering the sizzling fajitas.
sentences.zh: 假设一开始没有人点滋滋作响的法士达。

sentences.en: But then maybe about 20 minutes, 30 minutes into the dinner hour, and I've seen this,
sentences.zh: 但大约在晚餐进行了20分钟、30分钟后，我见过这种情况，

sentences.en: all of a sudden one person orders sizzling fajitas.
sentences.zh: 突然有一个人点了滋滋作响的法士达。

sentences.en: As the server brings out the sizzling skillet of fajita meat and onions.
sentences.zh: 当服务员端出滋滋冒油的法士达铁板和洋葱时。

sentences.en: And you hear that sizzling sound.
sentences.zh: 你听到了那种滋滋声。

sentences.en: Literally every eye, every single person in that restaurant,
sentences.zh: 真的，餐厅里的每一双眼睛、每一个人，

sentences.en: their head turns to the server walking past them.
sentences.zh: 他们的头都转向从身旁走过的服务员。

sentences.en: And they follow that server with their eyes.
sentences.zh: 他们的目光紧紧跟随那个服务员。

sentences.en: And then they smell the burnt onions.
sentences.zh: 接着你闻到了烤洋葱的香味。

sentences.en: And now you're hooked.
sentences.zh: 现在你被吸引住了。

sentences.en: And now everyone orders the sizzling fajitas.
sentences.zh: 紧接着所有人都开始点滋滋作响的法士达。

sentences.en: And in the back, instead of making that one order, they make 15.
sentences.zh: 后厨不仅要做那一份，还要做15份。

sentences.en: Yeah, they call it the fajita effect.
sentences.zh: 对，他们把这称为“法士达效应”。

sentences.en: My family fell victim to the fajita effect too many times to remember.
sentences.zh: 我的家人无数次沦为法士达效应的受害者。

sentences.en: We may even have initiated the original fajita effect.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可能引发了最初的法士达效应。

sentences.en: Patient zero of the fajita effect.
sentences.zh: 法士达效应的零号病人。

sentences.en: Chili's, by the way, did not invent the fajita.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，奇利餐厅并没有发明法士达。

sentences.en: That distinction goes to a Texan by the name of Sonny Falcone.
sentences.zh: 这个荣誉属于一个叫桑尼·法尔科内的德克萨斯人。

sentences.en: He was selling a subpar cut of meat called the faja.
sentences.zh: 他当时在卖一种劣质肉，叫做faja。

sentences.en: And figured that if you cooked it out in the open with a lot of spice,
sentences.zh: 他发现如果你把它露天烹饪并加入大量香料，

sentences.en: people didn't care about the quality of the meat.
sentences.zh: 人们就不在乎肉的质量了。

sentences.en: It got to Chili's because Larry Levine...
sentences.zh: 它传到奇利餐厅是因为拉里·莱文……

sentences.en: Larry Levine was the founder of Chili's.
sentences.zh: 拉里·莱文是奇利餐厅的创始人。

sentences.en: Had seen restaurants around the Rio Grande Valley sort of do their version of it.
sentences.zh: 他看到格兰德河谷周围的餐馆在做他们自己版本的法士达。

sentences.en: He had the idea to make sound the star of the show.
sentences.zh: 他萌生了让声音成为主角的想法。

sentences.en: And so when Chili's opened up,
sentences.zh: 所以在奇利餐厅开业时，

sentences.en: they put that sound of sizzling fajitas in their first ever commercial.
sentences.zh: 他们在他们的第一支商业广告中加入了法士达的滋滋声。

sentences.en: Fajitas sold like crazy.
sentences.zh: 法士达卖疯了。

sentences.en: In the wake of their massive success, Chili's printed up t-shirts for staff that said,
sentences.zh: 在其巨大成功之后，奇利餐厅为员工印制了T恤，上面写着：

sentences.en: I survived the summer of fajita madness.
sentences.zh: 我挺过了法士达疯狂之夏。

sentences.en: Now they serve enough fajita meat to fill two nuclear submarines a year.
sentences.zh: 现在他们每年供应的法士达肉量足以填满两艘核潜艇。

sentences.en: I really hope someone filled two nuclear submarines with fajita meat to get that measurement.
sentences.zh: 我真希望真的有人用法士达肉填满了两艘核潜艇来得出这个数据。

sentences.en: Tyler and Joel say it's surprisingly difficult to get people,
sentences.zh: 泰勒和乔尔说，让人——

sentences.en: even really creative people, to think about sound,
sentences.zh: 甚至是极具创意的人——去思考声音，

sentences.en: to value it in the same way they value the visual environment.
sentences.zh: 像重视视觉环境那样去重视声音，出奇地困难。

sentences.en: But sometimes there's one person who gets it.
sentences.zh: 但有时总有一个人能懂。

sentences.en: At Apple Computers, one of those people was a guy by the name of Jim Reeks.
sentences.zh: 在苹果电脑公司，这样的人之一是一个叫吉姆·里克斯的小伙子。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Jim Reeks.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫吉姆·里克斯。

sentences.en: I am the only person you know whose name is a complete sentence.
sentences.zh: 我是你认识的人中，唯一一个名字是一句完整句子的人。

sentences.en: Jim worked at Apple for about 10 years, starting in the late 80s.
sentences.zh: 吉姆在苹果工作了大约10年，从80年代末开始。

sentences.en: We didn't really have titles.
sentences.zh: 我们当时其实没有什么头衔。

sentences.en: I don't even think I had business cards.
sentences.zh: 我甚至觉得我都没有名片。

sentences.en: Well, whatever his title was,
sentences.zh: 好吧，不管他的头衔是什么，

sentences.en: Jim was working on sound for the Macintosh computers.
sentences.zh: 吉姆当时在为麦金塔电脑制作音效。

sentences.en: Which was a neglected stepchild of all things Mac.
sentences.zh: 这曾是所有Mac相关事物中备受冷落的继子。

sentences.en: No one really cared about the sound until the end,
sentences.zh: 直到最后，真的没人关心声音，

sentences.en: which is unfortunately typical.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这很典型。

sentences.en: Except Jim.
sentences.zh: 除了吉姆。

sentences.en: He's a composer and a musician,
sentences.zh: 他是一位作曲家兼音乐家，

sentences.en: and he understood the importance of sound more than most of his colleagues.
sentences.zh: 他比大多数同事都更能理解声音的重要性。

sentences.en: And Jim had strong feelings about the startup sound that was on the Mac at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且吉姆对当时Mac上的开机音有着强烈的感受。

sentences.en: I just hated it.
sentences.zh: 我简直恨透了它。

sentences.en: I just could not stand it.
sentences.zh: 我实在无法忍受。

sentences.en: Here's what it sounded like.
sentences.zh: 这就是它听起来的样子。

sentences.en: Here it is a couple more times, because it goes by really faSt.
sentences.zh: 再放几遍，因为它过得太快了。

sentences.en: So when Apple first started up, it was, you know, the computer was far from perfect.
sentences.zh: 所以当苹果刚开机时，你知道，电脑远非完美。

sentences.en: It crashed a lot.
sentences.zh: 它经常死机。

sentences.en: And every time you turned it back on, you heard that jolting sound.
sentences.zh: 每次你重新开机，都会听到那个刺耳的声音。

sentences.en: So Jim set out to make a better one.
sentences.zh: 于是吉姆着手制作一个更好的声音。

sentences.en: Your Mac just crashed.
sentences.zh: 你的Mac刚刚死机了。

sentences.en: Again.
sentences.zh: 又一次。

sentences.en: You've lost your work.
sentences.zh: 你的工作白干了。

sentences.en: Again.
sentences.zh: 又一次。

sentences.en: You're waiting for this thing to boot up.
sentences.zh: 你正在等这玩意儿启动。

sentences.en: Again.
sentences.zh: 又一次。

sentences.en: That's the audience.
sentences.zh: 这就是受众。

sentences.en: Just a bunch of pissed off, frustrated people who are super annoyed,
sentences.zh: 只是一群气急败坏、沮丧透顶、超级恼火的人，

sentences.en: and you're wasting their time.
sentences.zh: 而你在浪费他们的时间。

sentences.en: That's a hard audience to play to.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个很难讨好的受众。

sentences.en: I gotta change everyone's mood.
sentences.zh: 我得改变每个人的情绪。

sentences.en: So I was thinking a Zen-like meditative sound,
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在想一个禅宗般的冥想音效，

sentences.en: similar to a gong or chanting ohm.
sentences.zh: 类似于铜锣或哼唱“唵”。

sentences.en: Of course, we're all familiar with the sound he came up with.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们对后来他做出的那个声音都非常熟悉。

sentences.en: So much better, right?
sentences.zh: 好太多了，对吧？

sentences.en: Only problem was, Jim asked for permission to put this new sound into the prototype for the new Mac, and...
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是，吉姆请求把这个新声音放进新Mac的原型机里，结果……

sentences.en: I was told I couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 我被告知我不能这么做。

sentences.en: We already have a sound, you're not allowed to change it.
sentences.zh: 我们已经有一个声音了，不准换。

sentences.en: It was just on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 这种对话没完没了。

sentences.en: But Jim knew the people who were responsible for building the prototype.
sentences.zh: 但吉姆认识负责制造原型机的人。

sentences.en: I played it for them, and then they liked it.
sentences.zh: 我放给他们听，然后他们很喜欢。

sentences.en: And so when no one was around, we put it into the build.
sentences.zh: 所以在四下无人时，我们把它放进了系统版本中。

sentences.en: And the Quadra 700 shipped with the sound in it.
sentences.zh: Quadra 700带着这个声音出货了。

sentences.en: That was back in 1991, when the Quadra 700 Mac cost $6,000.
sentences.zh: 那是1991年，当时一台Quadra 700 Mac售价6000美元。

sentences.en: Jim says he never got any props for the sound, just grief.
sentences.zh: 吉姆说他没有因为这个声音得到任何赞赏，只有痛苦。

sentences.en: And yet, that sound, with a few minor tweaks, has been the Apple startup sound ever since.
sentences.zh: 然而，那个声音经过一些微调，从那以后就成了苹果的开机音。

sentences.en: So I think we can assume that Steve Jobs liked it.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们可以假设史蒂夫·乔布斯很喜欢它。

sentences.en: It's this big, giant, two-handed C chord, C major chord,
sentences.zh: 这是一个宏大、巨大、双手弹奏的C和弦，C大调和弦，

sentences.en: that makes you kind of feel welcome to this very stable, very substantial world of Apple.
sentences.zh: 它让你觉得有点受到欢迎，进入这个非常稳定、非常实质的苹果世界。

sentences.en: It's probably the single most connected sound with the Apple brand.
sentences.zh: 它可能是与苹果品牌联系最紧密的单一声音。

sentences.en: And brand is just the experience, or a perception prior to the experience.
sentences.zh: 而品牌就是体验，或者说体验之前的感知。

sentences.en: So everything that shapes the perception matters.
sentences.zh: 所以所有塑造这种感知的事物都至关重要。

sentences.en: It would be, you know, like, imagine a really beautiful car that just had this horrible engine always backfiring.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，想象一辆非常漂亮的汽车，却总是发出这种可怕的发动机回火声。

sentences.en: Actually, there are people who make sure that beautiful cars sound beautiful.
sentences.zh: 事实上，确实有人专门确保漂亮的汽车听起来也很美妙。

sentences.en: Or at least that they sound right.
sentences.zh: 或者至少让它们听起来对劲。

sentences.en: One of them is Sean Carney.
sentences.zh: 其中一位就是肖恩·卡尼。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Sean Carney.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫肖恩·卡尼。

sentences.en: I'm the Mustang powertrain sound quality engineer for Ford.
sentences.zh: 我是福特野马动力总成音质工程师。

sentences.en: Sean works on Mustangs, and there are all kinds of things he and his team can tweak to get the sound they're looking for.
sentences.zh: 肖恩负责野马汽车，他和他的团队可以通过各种方式进行微调，以获得他们想要的声音。

sentences.en: There's different tubes inside that the exhaust gases will flow through.
sentences.zh: 废气会流经内部不同的管道。

sentences.en: And those tubes have different shapes and different perforations, and they have different hole patterns in them.
sentences.zh: 这些管道有不同的形状和不同的穿孔，并且有不同的孔型。

sentences.en: It's sort of like an instrument.
sentences.zh: 这有点像一件乐器。

sentences.en: Kind of like you can control the sound of a horn by placing your fingers over different holes,
sentences.zh: 就像你可以通过把手指放在不同的孔上来控制号角的声音一样，

sentences.en: Sean can control the sound of the Mustang.
sentences.zh: 肖恩可以控制野马的声音。

sentences.en: And it's an easier job for the standard V8.
sentences.zh: 对于标准的V8发动机来说，这是一个相对简单的工作。

sentences.en: But then sometimes they'll put out a specialty Mustang.
sentences.zh: 但有时他们会推出特别版的野马。

sentences.en: In 2008, Mustang decided to put out a remake of a Mustang that appeared in the movie Bullet in 1968.
sentences.zh: 2008年，野马决定推出一款曾在1968年电影《警网铁金刚》（Bullitt）中出现过的野马的复刻版。

sentences.en: In the movie, there's a pretty famous chase sequence where Steve McQueen drives his Mustang all over the streets of San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 在电影中，有一个非常著名的追车片段，史蒂夫·麦奎因驾驶他的野马穿梭于旧金山的街道。

sentences.en: Sean and his team wanted to make the 2008 Bullet sound similar to the 1968 Bullet.
sentences.zh: 肖恩和他的团队希望让2008款的Bullitt听起来像1968款的一样。

sentences.en: So when it comes to a car like a Bullet, it's about an old car from the old movie.
sentences.zh: 所以当谈到像Bullitt这样的车时，它是关于老电影里的一辆老车。

sentences.en: So yeah, we're trying to make that specific car speak to you in a way.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们正试图让那辆特定的车以某种方式与你对话。

sentences.en: It's drawing you back into those old memories.
sentences.zh: 它把你拉回到那些旧的回忆中。

sentences.en: It's almost like that folklore of what that car might have been.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是关于那辆车可能是什么样的一种民间传说。

sentences.en: They're trying essentially to make a new car sound old,
sentences.zh: 他们本质上是试图让一辆新车听起来像旧车，

sentences.en: which is challenging because cars made in 1968 were built completely differently.
sentences.zh: 这很有挑战性，因为1968年制造的汽车结构完全不同。

sentences.en: That old engine had a carburetor.
sentences.zh: 那台老发动机有化油器。

sentences.en: We use a fuel injection system.
sentences.zh: 我们使用的是燃油喷射系统。

sentences.en: And all those things, they completely change how the engine can sound.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素完全改变了发动机的声音。

sentences.en: Sean was never going to be able to duplicate the sound of the Bullet car from the movie exactly.
sentences.zh: 肖恩本来就不可能完全复制电影中那辆“警网铁金刚”汽车的声音。

sentences.en: For one, the Mustang in the movie was enhanced with sounds recorded from a race car.
sentences.zh: 一方面，电影里的野马跑车是用从赛车上录制的声音进行过增强的。

sentences.en: And apart from that, it's actually illegal in most places to drive around in a car that loud.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，在大多数地方，开着这么大声音的车上路其实是违法的。

sentences.en: So a big part of what we try to do is we try to identify key characteristics.
sentences.zh: 所以我们尝试做的大部分工作，就是努力识别出关键特征。

sentences.en: What are the notes that are being played by that classic American V8 sound that's in the movie?
sentences.zh: 电影中那种经典美国V8发动机的声音弹奏出的音符到底是什么？

sentences.en: When the reviews of the Bullet Mustang came out, people talked about the sound.
sentences.zh: 当《警网铁金刚》野马跑车的评论出来时，人们都在讨论它的声音。

sentences.en: And most people thought Sean and his team had gotten it right.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数人认为肖恩和他的团队做得很棒。

sentences.en: Here's the 2008 Bullet Mustang in action.
sentences.zh: 这就是2008款“警网铁金刚”野马跑车在行驶中的表现。

sentences.en: Sound is actually, in terms of all of our senses, it's the one we react to quickeSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就我们所有的感官而言，声音是我们反应最快的。

sentences.en: It's even quicker than touch.
sentences.zh: 它甚至比触觉还要快。

sentences.en: That's Joel Beckerman again.
sentences.zh: 这又是乔尔·贝克曼说的。

sentences.en: Brands that are not paying attention to this,
sentences.zh: 那些不注意这一点的品牌，

sentences.en: not paying attention to sound in association with experiences,
sentences.zh: 不注意声音与体验相联系的品牌，

sentences.en: they're really going to get punished.
sentences.zh: 它们真的会受到惩罚。

sentences.en: Case in point, in 2010, Frito-Lay decided to come out with a new biodegradable SunChips bag.
sentences.zh: 一个典型的例子是，2010年，菲多利公司决定推出一种全新的可生物降解的太阳薯片包装袋。

sentences.en: Only problem was they never considered what that packaging sounded like.
sentences.zh: 唯一的缺点是，他们从来没有考虑过这种包装袋发出的声音是怎样的。

sentences.en: Here's a YouTube video someone made about the bag.
sentences.zh: 这是某人在YouTube上制作的关于这个袋子的视频。

sentences.en: Delicious SunChips.
sentences.zh: 美味的太阳薯片。

sentences.en: Love all your products.
sentences.zh: 我爱你们所有的产品。

sentences.en: The thing that I cannot get over is the noise that this bag makes.
sentences.zh: 我最无法释怀的是这个袋子发出的噪音。

sentences.en: I don't know what it's made out of.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它是什么材料做的。

sentences.en: If you ever wanted to get, like, just one little chip out of the bag,
sentences.zh: 如果你想从袋子里拿出一小片薯片，

sentences.en: I'm actually yelling, and you probably can't remember.
sentences.zh: 我其实是在大喊大叫，你可能都记不清了。

sentences.en: If you want to get one chip out of this bag, good luck.
sentences.zh: 如果你想从这个袋子里拿出一片薯片，祝你好运。

sentences.en: That guy on YouTube was not the only person to notice how noisy the bag was.
sentences.zh: YouTube上的那个家伙并不是唯一一个注意到这个袋子有多吵的人。

sentences.en: Someone created a Facebook page called,
sentences.zh: 有人创建了一个名为

sentences.en: Sorry I Can't Hear You Over This SunChips Bag,
sentences.zh: “抱歉，这个太阳薯片袋子的声音太大，我听不见你说话”的Facebook主页，

sentences.en: and it got 40,000 likes, and it became a national news story.
sentences.zh: 它获得了4万个赞，并成为全国新闻报道的焦点。

sentences.en: They had to pull the new bag and go back to the old bag.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不撤回新包装袋，换回旧包装袋。

sentences.en: Good intentions.
sentences.zh: 好意。

sentences.en: Bad execution.
sentences.zh: 糟糕的执行。

sentences.en: Joel and Tyler refer to this kind of sound as sonic trash.
sentences.zh: 乔尔和泰勒把这种声音称为声音垃圾。

sentences.en: You know, you'd never let somebody take a bunch of trash and throw it in your front lawn.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你绝不会让别人把一堆垃圾扔在你的前院草坪上。

sentences.en: But we allow cities, our neighbors, brands, to really invade our sonic space.
sentences.zh: 但我们却允许城市、我们的邻居以及品牌肆意侵入我们的声音空间。

sentences.en: To dump garbage in your ear?
sentences.zh: 把垃圾倾倒在你的耳朵里？

sentences.en: Is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: Essentially, essentially.
sentences.zh: 基本上，基本上是这样。

sentences.en: Joel and Tyler imagine a world where all the sounds we hear have more thought behind them,
sentences.zh: 乔尔和泰勒设想了一个世界，在那里我们听到的一切声音都融入了更多的思考，

sentences.en: more intention.
sentences.zh: 更多的意图。

sentences.en: It would be very rare that you would actually hear the sound that something made.
sentences.zh: 你实际上很少会直接听到某个东西原本发出的声音。

sentences.en: That thing would trigger a better sound.
sentences.zh: 那个东西会触发一个更好的声音。

sentences.en: In Tyler's world, they could make the SunChips Bag sound like this when it's opened.
sentences.zh: 在泰勒的世界里，他们可以让太阳薯片袋在打开时听起来像这样。

sentences.en: Every time you get a chip, you're like,
sentences.zh: 每次你拿一块薯片，你就会想，

sentences.en: Yeah, except that sound.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，除了那个声音。

sentences.en: It's actually on that very short list of trademark sounds.
sentences.zh: 它实际上在那份极短的商标声音名单上。

sentences.en: So hands off.
sentences.zh: 所以不准碰。

sentences.en: Whatever.
sentences.zh: 随便吧。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Katie Mingle with Sam Greenspan,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由凯蒂·明格尔与萨姆·格林斯潘、

sentences.en: Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 艾弗里·特拉夫曼以及我罗曼·马斯共同制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 local public radio KALW in San Francisco
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7地方公共广播电台KALW的一个项目，

sentences.en: and produced of the Offices of ArcSign,
sentences.zh: 由位于美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心的建筑与室内设计公司ArcSign事务所制作。

sentences.en: an architecture and interiors firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 这是一个位于美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心的建筑与室内设计公司。

sentences.en: I hope when I die, there's a button on my tombstone
sentences.zh: 我希望当我死后，我的墓碑上有一个按钮，

sentences.en: and you can press it and it would play the sound.
sentences.zh: 你可以按一下，它就会播放声音。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到这个节目并为之点赞。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我在推特上@罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: We also have a cool Tumblr and a Spotify playlist
sentences.zh: 我们还有一个很酷的Tumblr和一个Spotify播放列表，

sentences.en: that will provide a nice soundtrack to your workday.
sentences.zh: 它将为你的工作日提供美妙的背景音乐。

sentences.en: But I encourage you to explore the entire world of 99% Invisible
sentences.zh: 但我鼓励你在99pi.org上探索《99%隐形》的整个世界。

sentences.en: at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 网址是99pi.org。

sentences.en: Videotopia.
sentences.zh: 录像带乌托邦。
